steps.label: Application object
steps.sub: global, tenant-independent definition — name, required permissions, credentials

steps.label: Service principal
steps.sub: tenant-local identity that actually authenticates and holds RBAC assignments

steps.label: Multi-tenant apps
steps.sub: one application object, a separate service principal in every consenting tenant

code:
# 1. Federated credential (workload identity federation)
#    OIDC token from GitHub Actions / Kubernetes / another cloud
#    exchanged for an Entra ID token -- NO secret stored, ever
#
# 2. Certificate
#    private key harder to leak than plain text; normal PKI lifecycle
#
# 3. Client secret (last resort)
#    shortest tolerable expiration, stored in Key Vault, rotated
#    by the pipeline -- the most common root cause of SP compromise
caption: Prefer the top of this list whenever the calling platform supports it.

eyebrow: No credential to leak at all

steps.label: System-assigned
steps.sub: 1:1 with the resource -- delete the VM or function app, the identity goes with it

steps.label: User-assigned
steps.sub: standalone resource, its own lifecycle, attachable to many resources at once

steps.label: Behind the scenes
steps.sub: platform rotates the credential via the Instance Metadata Service -- code never sees a secret

code:
# Managed identity that reads secrets from one Key Vault:
#
#   WRONG:  Contributor on the resource group
#   RIGHT:  Key Vault Secrets User, scoped to that one vault
#
# If the workload is ever compromised, the attacker is bounded
# by exactly what you scoped the identity to -- nothing more.
caption: Same RBAC discipline as Lesson 7, applied to non-human identities.
